description: This chapter traces how geometry evolved from ancient land-measuring practices into a formal mathematical system built on definitions, axioms, and postulates. It introduces Euclid's framework — the foundation of all the geometry you'll study in school — and shows how mathematicians use deductive reasoning to prove theorems from basic assumptions.

sections.title: 5.1 Introduction
sections.summary: Historical origins of geometry across ancient civilisations (Egypt, India, Greece) leading to Euclid's systematic approach

sections.title: 5.2 Euclid's Definitions, Axioms and Postulates
sections.summary: Euclid's foundational definitions (point, line, surface), axioms (universal truths), five postulates (geometry-specific assumptions), worked examples, and Theorem 5.1

subsections.title: Definitions (Solids to Points)
subsections.summary: Euclid's 7 key definitions from Book 1, the problem of infinite regress, and why point/line/plane are left undefined

subsections.title: Axioms (Common Notions)
subsections.summary: Seven universal axioms (equality, addition, subtraction, coincidence, whole-part, doubles, halves) and their application to magnitudes

subsections.title: Postulates (Five Geometry Assumptions)
subsections.summary: Euclid's five postulates with special focus on the complexity of Postulate 5 (parallel lines), and Axiom 5.1 (unique line through two points)

subsections.title: Consistent Systems and Theorems
subsections.summary: Definition of a consistent axiomatic system, deductive reasoning chain, and Theorem 5.1 (two distinct lines share at most one point)

subsections.title: Worked Examples
subsections.summary: Example 1 (AB + BC = AC using Axiom 4), Example 2 (equilateral triangle construction using Postulate 3)

sections.title: EXERCISE 5.1
sections.summary: Seven practice questions testing true/false reasoning, term definitions, postulate analysis, midpoint proofs, and segment equality proofs

sections.title: 5.3 Summary
sections.summary: Recap of the seven key points — undefined terms, axioms/postulates as unproven assumptions, theorems as proved statements, list of axioms and postulates
